title: Autonomic Nervous System Regulation and Acute Stress Markers
source_organization: American Autonomic Society / NASA Life Sciences
author: Task Force on Heart Rate Variability
population_studied: Healthy adults and extreme environment operators
excerpt: Acute physiological stress induces simultaneous sympathetic activation and parasympathetic vagal withdrawal. This autonomic state is characterized by an elevated instantaneous heart rate, marked reduction in beat-to-beat variability (RMSSD collapse below 20 ms), and rapid bursts of skin conductance (phasic EDA spikes). Resting RMSSD reflecting cardiac parasympathetic tone must be distinguished from transient task-related reductions.

title: Thermoregulatory Dynamics and Core-to-Peripheral Heat Flux
author: Thermal Physiology Research Group
population_studied: Human endurance athletes and aerospace crews
excerpt: Peripheral skin temperature exhibits gradual thermodynamic drift under steady ambient conditions. Acute rates of change exceeding 0.50 C/min indicate rapid environmental displacement, intense evaporative cooling, or severe cutaneous vasoconstriction due to acute adrenergic surges. Baseline normothermic skin temperature typically ranges from 32.5 C to 35.0 C depending on skin-contact sensor placement.
